22. Implementation Theory

Can a desired social choice rule be "implemented" as the outcome of Nash equilibrium — see the mandatory screening test, Maskin monotonicity, with your own eyes.

  • Maskin Monotonicity — Two agents, three alternatives X={a,b,c}X = \{a, b, c\}X={a,b,c}. If a rule fff picks xxx at θ\thetaθ and xxx falls for no one at θ′\theta'θ′, then f(θ′)f(\theta')f(θ′) must still be xxx — a necessary condition for Nash implementation. The dictatorial rule passes; the bottom-choice rule earns a red violation.
